inviolable_rules.description: These three rules are absolute. If a wave count violates any of them, the count is wrong and must be discarded. No exceptions.

rule_1.name: WAVE_2_CANNOT_RETRACE_BELOW_WAVE_1_START
rule_1.statement: Wave 2 can never retrace 100% or more of Wave 1. It may retrace up to 99.9% of Wave 1, but a single tick below the start of Wave 1 invalidates the count.
rule_1.implication: This rule defines the absolute stop loss level for any Wave 2 trade. Place the stop one tick below the origin of Wave 1.
rule_1.common_miscount: Deep corrections that breach Wave 1 origin are often Wave A-B-C corrections of a larger degree, not Wave 2.

rule_2.name: WAVE_3_CANNOT_BE_THE_SHORTEST_IMPULSE_WAVE
rule_2.statement: Wave 3 can never be the shortest impulse wave when compared to Waves 1 and 5. It must be longer than at least one of the other two impulse waves. Note: Wave 3 does not have to be the longest — it just cannot be the shortest.
rule_2.implication: When measuring waves, if Wave 3 appears shorter than both Wave 1 and Wave 5, the count is incorrect.
rule_2.common_miscount: Confusing an extended Wave 1 or Wave 5 with Wave 3. If Wave 5 is very long, verify Wave 3 is still not the shortest.

rule_3.name: WAVE_4_CANNOT_OVERLAP_WAVE_1_PRICE_TERRITORY
rule_3.statement: In a standard impulse wave, Wave 4 cannot enter the price territory of Wave 1. The low of Wave 4 (in a bull market) must not fall below the high of Wave 1.
rule_3.implication: If Wave 4 overlaps Wave 1, the structure is not a standard impulse. It may be a diagonal triangle or the count is wrong.
rule_3.exception: The only exception is a diagonal triangle (wedge) pattern, where overlap between Waves 1 and 4 is permitted by definition.

wave_personality.description: Each wave in the Elliott Wave sequence has a characteristic personality reflecting the underlying mass psychology driving price action.

wave_1.name: The Stealth Wave
characteristics: Least obvious wave — hard to identify in real time.
Begins at the end of the previous trend as early adopters and smart money enter.
Volume is modest, sentiment is still bearish (in a new uptrend).
Fundamental news is still negative — the move seems counter-intuitive.
Often appears as a relief rally rather than the start of a new trend.
wave_1.trader_psychology: Most traders dismiss Wave 1 as a dead-cat bounce or short-covering. Only contrarians and early-trend followers participate.

wave_2.name: The Doubt Wave
characteristics: Corrects Wave 1, often retracing 50-78.6% of Wave 1.
Volume contracts significantly during this correction.
Sentiment turns negative again — many believe the original downtrend has resumed.
Often forms as a Zigzag (A-B-C) correction.
Creates a higher low (in an uptrend), which is the first sign of trend change.
wave_2.trader_psychology: Fear returns. Late sellers re-enter short. This creates the fuel for the powerful Wave 3 that follows.

wave_3.name: The Momentum Wave
characteristics: Typically the longest and most powerful wave.
Strong volume expansion — institutional participation is high.
Fundamental news begins to confirm the new trend direction.
Breakouts from consolidation zones are common in this wave.
Hard and fast moves with minimal pullbacks.
Most profitable wave to trade — clear direction, strong momentum.
wave_3.trader_psychology: The majority of traders recognize the trend and FOMO (fear of missing out) drives aggressive participation. Momentum traders join.

wave_4.name: The Rest Wave
characteristics: Complex, overlapping correction — often sideways rather than sharp.
Commonly forms as flats, triangles, or combinations (unlike the sharper Wave 2 Zigzag).
Volume is lower than Wave 3.
Sentiment is mixed — bulls take profits, bears attempt reversals.
Provides base for Wave 5 launch — often finds support at Wave 1 high (polarity).
wave_4.trader_psychology: Traders who missed Wave 3 look to buy the dip but are frustrated by choppy, sideways action. Patience is tested.

wave_5.name: The Exhaustion Wave
characteristics: Final leg of the impulse — driven by sentiment rather than fundamentals.
Breadth narrows — fewer instruments participate in the rally.
Volume often diverges (lower than Wave 3) — a warning sign.
RSI and momentum indicators frequently show bearish divergence.
Retail euphoria peaks — 'this time is different' narrative dominates.
Often extends to 100% of Wave 1 length or Fibonacci extensions (1.272, 1.618 of Wave 1-3).
wave_5.trader_psychology: Maximum optimism and public participation at the exact wrong time. The smart money distributes into retail buying.

wave_A.name: The Denial Wave
characteristics: First leg of the correction after the impulse.
Many traders believe it is just a brief pullback within the trend.
Bearish in a bull market — sharp initial decline.
Volume picks up as longs exit and early bears enter.

wave_B.name: The False Hope Wave
characteristics: Counter-trend bounce within the correction.
Volume is lower than Wave A — the rally is unconvincing.
Creates illusion that the uptrend has resumed.
Often ends below the Wave 5 high — a lower high.
Traps bulls who buy the 'dip' thinking the trend continues.
Can be complex and prolonged, testing patience.

wave_C.name: The Capitulation Wave
characteristics: Final and most damaging leg of the correction.
Strong, impulsive character — 5 sub-waves within it.
Forces final liquidation of longs who survived Wave A and B.
Maximum pessimism — often ends at or near the Wave 4 territory of the previous impulse.
Volume surges as panic selling climaxes.
Ends the corrective structure — new impulse begins from here.

fibonacci_relationships.description: Elliott Waves have natural Fibonacci ratio relationships that aid in projecting wave targets and validating counts.

impulse_relationships.wave_3_vs_wave_1: Most commonly 161.8% of Wave 1. Can extend to 261.8% or 423.6% of Wave 1
impulse_relationships.wave_5_vs_wave_1: Commonly equal to Wave 1 in length (100%), or 61.8% of Waves 1-3 combined

corrective_relationships.wave_A: No fixed ratio — marks start of correction
corrective_relationships.wave_B_vs_wave_A: Typically retraces 38.2%, 50%, or 61.8% of Wave A
corrective_relationships.wave_C_vs_wave_A: Commonly equal to Wave A (100%) or 161.8% of Wave A

wave_3_entries.description: Wave 3 is the highest-probability trade in Elliott Wave theory. The agent strategy for Wave 3 entries:
setup_requirements: Confirm a 5-wave impulse structure has completed on a higher timeframe (the previous trend).
Identify Wave 1 of the new impulse — a sharp move against the prior trend.
Wait for Wave 2 correction to retrace to the 38.2%-78.6% Fibonacci zone of Wave 1.
Confirm Wave 2 correction is complete (momentum shift, rejection candle, or 5-wave A-B-C structure in Wave 2).
Enter at the end of Wave 2 with stop below the origin of Wave 1.
Target: 161.8% extension of Wave 1 from the Wave 2 low as the primary Wave 3 target.
confidence_conditions: Wave 2 retracement aligns with a high-quality S/R zone
Wave 2 forms a classic A-B-C Zigzag structure
Volume expanded on Wave 1 and contracted on Wave 2
Fibonacci retracement of Wave 2 aligns with the 0.618 level

wave_5_exhaustion_warnings.description: Wave 5 trades are lower probability. The agent issues exhaustion warnings rather than entry signals in most Wave 5 scenarios.
warning_triggers: Price reaches 100% or 127.2% extension of Wave 1 from Wave 2 low
RSI or MACD shows bearish divergence while price makes new high
Volume is noticeably lower than the Wave 3 peak
Sentiment indicators show extreme bullishness (e.g., fear/greed index above 80)
The impulse wave count reaches Wave 5 on multiple timeframes simultaneously
wave_5_exhaustion_warnings.agent_action: Issue a WAVE_5_EXHAUSTION_WARNING flag. Tighten stops on existing long positions. Reduce new long exposure. Begin monitoring for Wave A setup.
wave_5_exhaustion_warnings.prohibited_action: The agent must not initiate new long positions at Wave 5 exhaustion zones. Counter-trend shorts require strong confirmation and reduced size.
